title: 建築家の森俊子氏に金メダル　米芸術文学アカデミーが選出　イサム・ノグチ賞の受賞者
extracted_text: 米国の芸術、文学などの分野で最も権威がある米芸術文学アカデミーは3日までに、生涯の業績に対して与える功労賞である建築部門の「金メダル」に、ハーバード大大学院デザイン研究科教授で建築家の森俊子氏を選んだと発表した。 森氏は1951年、神戸市生まれ。2002～08年同研究科の建築学科長を務めた。ニューヨークで自身の建築設計事務所を主宰し、代表作はニューヨーク・ブルックリン公共図書館やアフリカ・セネガルの文化センターなど。21年にはイサム・ノグチ賞を受賞した。 アカデミーは1898年設立。現役の芸術家や作家、音楽家、建築家ら300人の終身会員で構成される。森氏は2020年から会員。各部門の最高の栄誉である金メダルは、年ごとに異なる部門から選出され、今年は建築と歴史部門から選ばれた。（共同）
translated_text: The American Academy of Arts and Letters, the most authoritative institution in the fields of art and literature in the United States, announced by the 3rd that it has selected Professor Toshiko Mori, an architect and professor at Harvard University's Graduate School of Design, for the Gold Medal in the architecture department, a merit award given for lifetime achievements. Mori was born in Kobe City in 1951. She served as chair of the architecture department at the same graduate school from 2002 to 2008. She runs her own architectural design firm in New York, with notable works including the Brooklyn Public Library in New York and the Cultural Center in Senegal, Africa. In 2021, she received the Isamu Noguchi Prize. The Academy was founded in 1898 and consists of 300 Lifetime Members who are active artists, writers, musicians, and architects. Mori has been a member since 2020. The Gold Medal, the highest honor in each department, is selected from a different department each year, and this year it was chosen from the architecture and historical departments. (Kyodo)
title_en: Architect Toshiko Mori Selected for Gold Medal by American Academy of Arts and Letters; Winner of Isamu Noguchi Prize
